summary: Added active network discovery scanning to myiotsan, the counterpart to the existing MQTT enrollment window: an admin can now sweep the LAN instead of only waiting for a device to announce itself. New package infra/iot/discover normalises every scanner to a shared Found type: ScanModbus (a gentle subnet sweep -- a cheap TCP :502 connect probe before it ever walks unit ids on a host, then SunSpec auto-identification via the existing sunspec.Discover for vendor/model/serial, falling back to an 'unidentified Modbus' candidate when a device answers but isn't SunSpec-compliant), ScanMDNS (browses common DNS-SD service types via a new pure-Go dependency, github.com/hashicorp/mdns, pulling in github.com/miekg/dns -- Chromecast/HomeKit/Shelly/printers etc.), ScanSSDP (UDP 1900 M-SEARCH for Sonos/Roku/DLNA), ScanEtherNetIP (UDP 44818 ListIdentity broadcast for Rockwell/CIP PLCs), and ScanBACnet (UDP 47808 Who-Is broadcast for building-automation controllers) -- plus a Hosts helper that expands a CIDR into a flat host list capped at 1024 addresses so a fat subnet mask can never launch a runaway sweep. On the app side, a new ScanService (apps/myiotsan/services/scanner.go) orchestrates the requested scanners and records every Found as the SAME quarantined DiscoveredDevice candidate the MQTT announce path already produces -- a scan never adds a device, it only proposes candidates an admin then adopts through the identical review step, deduped by a synthetic device key so re-scanning refreshes rather than duplicates, and audited to the notification feed exactly like opening an enrollment window. DiscoveredDevice gained Source/Address/Endpoint/Unit/Transport fields, and adopting a Modbus-scan candidate now carries its connection straight into the created device (services.Enrollment.Adopt) so it starts polling immediately with no manual re-typing. New route POST /api/discovery/scan (admin-only, under the already-admin-only /discovery prefix). Frontend gained a Scan panel on the Discovery page (per-protocol toggles plus CIDR/transport/units for the Modbus sweep) and a scan-aware candidate card showing how a candidate was found and its address instead of a topic. Every scanner is opt-in (admin-triggered), bounded (host cap, per-scan timeout, concurrency cap), strictly read-only (no scanner ever writes to a device), and LAN-local. Verified live end to end for Modbus/mDNS/SSDP (scan -> SunSpec-identify -> candidate with endpoint/unit prefilled and generic-sunspec-solar suggested -> adopt -> device; mDNS/SSDP ran against a real LAN without error); EtherNet/IP and BACnet are parser-verified only against synthetic protocol-mock byte frames, since no real PLC was available in CI -- see docs/DISCOVERY_SCANNING.md for the honest per-scanner verification status and what was deliberately deferred (OPC-UA discovery, Profinet DCP, a Matter controller, native TV/AV control) and why. Alongside this, a small label fix: the profile editor's Transport option now reads 'Modbus' instead of 'Modbus TCP', and its hint clarifies that the connection (Modbus TCP / RTU-over-TCP / serial) is chosen per device, since that axis is really the protocol family (MQTT vs Modbus), not the wire transport.
compatibility: Fully additive; nothing about the existing MQTT enrollment window, its candidate table, or the adoption flow changes for a site that never runs a scan. The new DiscoveredDevice.Source/Address/Endpoint/Unit/Transport columns default empty/zero and existing MQTT-sourced candidate rows are unaffected. The two new Go dependencies (github.com/hashicorp/mdns, github.com/miekg/dns) are pure-Go, add no new listening port, and are only exercised when an admin explicitly runs a scan that includes mDNS -- POST /api/discovery/scan is admin-only and does nothing until called. No database migration: the new columns are added by the existing code-first ORM the same way any other entity field change is. The Transport label/hint change is a frontend-only i18n text edit (en/ms/zh/ar) with no behavioral effect.
